#1721. Friday's UEFA Nations League predictions including Serbia vs. Germany, Netherlands vs. Greece

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 00:05, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 00:05

Today's UEFA Nations League predictions include Serbia's clash with Germany, and a contest between Netherlands and Greece.

Moldova and Kazakhstan will continue their respective 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaigns with a contest in Group C3 on Friday night.

Neither team can finish at the top of the section and secure automatic promotion to League B, but the pair are both in the running to qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Both teams are searching for valuable wins in Group C3, but the pair might have to settle for a share of the spoils in this Nations League fixture.

> Click here to read our full preview for Moldova vs. Kazakhstan, including team news and predicted lineups

Andorra will conclude their Nations League D campaign on Friday, when they welcome Gibraltar to Estadi de la FAF d'Encamp.

The hosts are last in their three-team group with one point from their three matches so far, whereas the visitors are second with two points from two games.

Neither side are likely to be at their best considering there is little to play for given all teams will be in Nations League C.

However, with Andorra backed by a home crowd, perhaps the hosts will be able take at least a point against Gibraltar, who have often travelled poorly.

> Click here to read our full preview for Andorra vs. Gibraltar, including team news and predicted lineups

Looking to secure their first UEFA Nations League victory in more than six years, Liechtenstein welcome Azerbaijan to the Rheinpark Stadion on Friday night.

The hosts are preparing for their penultimate group-stage fixture, while this will be the fourth and final match of the campaign for Aykhan Abbasov's side.

With Azerbaijan enjoying their best run of form for several years, they will be keen to close out the Nations League in positive fashion.

We see the away side coming away with three points and securing another 1-0 win over Liechtenstein.

> Click here to read our full preview for Azerbaijan vs. Liechtenstein, including team news and predicted lineups

Kosicka Futbalova Arena will be the backdrop for a crucial showdown between two unbeaten teams in UEFA Nations League C's Group 3 on Friday, when Slovakia host Faroe Islands.

The Falcons could earn a fourth win in five games, though Landslidid will be motivated by the possibility of promotion.

Slovakia are the favourites owing to the superior quality in their squad, and their 81-better FIFA ranking, though they are unlikely to pull off a second consecutive thrashing.

Faroe Islands are the only nation that have caused the Falcons to drop points in Group C3, so expect to see another close-fought contest between two unbeaten sides.

> Click here to read our full preview for Slovakia vs. Faroe Islands, including team news and predicted lineups

Iceland could clinch promotion to Nations League C by beating hosts Bulgaria on Friday at Stadion Hristo Botev.

The Icelandic national team are currently top of Group C with eight points from four matchdays, whereas their opponents are third with four points and must win if they are to make certain that they remain in the race for promotion.

Though home advantage has often been crucial for many teams, Bulgaria have struggled for consistency when playing as hosts.

Iceland have also performed well on their travels in the Nations League, and they should be confident that they can take three points on Friday.

> Click here to read our full preview for Bulgaria vs. Iceland, including team news and predicted lineups

Estonia square off against Luxembourg on Friday evening knowing that victory could guarantee them a top-two spot in UEFA Nations League Group C4.

However, despite sitting bottom of the group, Luxembourg can move level on points with their second-placed opponents with a win in Luxembourg City.

With Estonia having shown their defensive quality at this level, it will be difficult for Luxembourg to get on the scoresheet. After Estonia beat Luxembourg by the solitary goal in their first meeting in October, we feel that a repeat scoreline could occur here.

> Click here to read our full preview for Luxembourg vs. Estonia, including team news and predicted lineups

Scotland and North Macedonia will clash at Hampden Park on Friday night in UEFA Nations League B Group 1.

The hosts are third in the standings with four points, while the visitors are bottom of the table and yet to pick up a single point from four matches.

Scotland may be enduring a difficult run, but they demonstrated their superiority over the struggling North Macedonia in the reverse fixture and should secure another comfortable win on Friday.

By Lewis Nolan | 13 Nov 2026 00:28

Mauricio Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year deal to become the next Manchester United manager, the newest report has revealed.

After leaving the Red Devils 18th in the Premier League table with just eight points from their first 10 matches, it came as no surprise to anyone to see the club sack Michael Carrick on Thursday.

He became the seventh permanent manager to lose his job since the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, and fans will hope that the next boss can be the one to finally bring the team back to the pinnacle of English football.

Pochettino was widely reported to be the frontrunner, even ahead of candidates like Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann.

The Athletic have revealed that the Argentine is set to sign a contract until 2029, and his first game will come against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

A win at Anfield against Liverpool would be the best possible start to life as United boss for Pochettino, but there are concerns about how long he will have to prepare for that match.

The 54-year-old is expected to take charge of the USA national team for the country's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final legs against Haiti.

Those clashes will take place on Saturday and on Wednesday, while the Red Devils will face Liverpool on Sunday, meaning he will have very little time to prepare his squad for their clash against their biggest rivals.

Many thought that Carrick would be dismissed weeks ago, so the fact that United have waited until now to agree a deal with Pochettino is yet another indictment on the chaos behind the scenes at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will need grace given United are arguably at their lowest ever period since Ferguson's retirement, but fans should be excited about the club's next manager.

The 54-year-old's Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton sides were some of the hardest working teams in Europe, and that type of intensity has long been missing at Old Trafford.

If Pochettino can change the culture in training and in the squad, that could have a lasting effect beyond his tenure in Manchester.

The only question is whether the Argentine will be backed sufficiently by the decision makers above him, as if he is let down by the likes of Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, then United's ceiling under him will be capped.

#1714. Rio Ferdinand claps back at fans mocking him for celebrating Man United's late equaliser against Aston Villa which left them in the relegation zone

Published: 14:15 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:16 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at football fans who criticised his reaction on social media to Manchester United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Former United defender Ferdinand drew criticism when he shared a photo of himself celebrating after the Red Devils' dramatic comeback on Sunday afternoon.

Michael Carrick's side had looked down and out at 4-2 in stoppage time, but late strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu meant they earned a point from the game.

They did, though, remain in the relegation zone – however Ferdinand shared two snaps to his X account following full-time.

The first showed the 48-year-old with his head in his hands, and the second saw him celebrating. He captioned the post: 'From this to THIS!!! Carrick time!!!!!!!!!! Birthday weekend just got (a) tad better in the last 6 minutes…'

Fans though flooded the replies with criticism, questioning why he was 'celebrating a draw' and calling him an 'embarrassment'. Ferdinand, though, has now taken the opportunity to respond.

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at fans who criticised his response to Manchester United's draw with Aston Villa

'Let me just address something,' Ferdinand began on Rio Ferdinand Presents. 'On socials I put a picture up and little comment underneath of me going like that (celebrates).

'That's not me celebrating a point against Aston Villa, by the way, it's me celebrating a moment in a football match. It's what football does to you. It can take over your body, take over your emotions in a moment. That moment isn't the big picture.

'So all of these people saying his standards have dropped and he's celebrating a draw... I'm not celebrating a draw against Villa, I'm celebrating the moment and the fact we actually came back and showed a bit of character.

'It's always about that moment that when you calm down and you go, look where we are in the league, that's terrible, looks how things unfolded in the game, that needs work. But, in the moment, as a football fan, you are allowed to get carried away with it.

'That's what football does. If you don't know that or don't understand it or feel it, you're not a football person, so get out.'

Ferdinand hasn't shied away from criticising his former team-mate Carrick amid United's poor run of form that has left them in 18th in the Premier League table.

United came back from behind to draw 4-4 with Villa having looked down and out in the game

His assessment of Sunday's showing was more tame, with the ex-centre back describing the effort as full of both character and chaos.

He added: 'It's like we need a punch on the nose, or two or three, to start playing. But then, the flip side of it, it's character and ability plays a part in that.

'In the end, we could have won it. But they are giving us fans grey hairs. It's crazy football.'

As thrilling as Man United's fight-back may have been to some fans, manager Carrick was still forced to answer difficult questions at full-time.

Sky Sports' Patrick Davison asked the former captain what he 'expected to happen over the next few weeks' - suggesting a question mark still lingering over his tenure despite comebacks against Roma and Villa.

Carrick's response was understandably thorny, with the manager underlining that he 'probably' would not be walking away from the role.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week.

#1710. Romania vs Poland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 13 Nov 2026 01:20, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 18:30

Romania and Poland will lock horns at the Arena Nationala in Bucharest on Saturday night, with both nations desperate to get their UEFA Nations League campaigns back on track.

Pressure is mounting on both managers, while the threat of relegation from League B adds further intrigue to an already tasty contest.

When Gheorghe Hagi returned to take charge of the Romanian national team last April, he brought with him a wave of optimism, although that feel-good factor has proved remarkably short-lived.

Less than six months into his reign, the Tricolours find themselves in the middle of a full-blown meltdown, with problems extending well beyond their disappointing results on the pitch.

Hagi initially took aim at the Romanian media ahead of the Nations League campaign, accusing journalists of being overly pessimistic before boldly predicting that his side would collect all 12 points from their opening four matches.

Reality has been less kind, with Romania losing all four encounters while shipping 13 goals in the process.

Putting aside the on-field problems, there have been a series of bitter public exchanges between Hagi and high-profile members of the Romanian national team - especially in the last few days.

Nicolae Stanciu, for example, was accused by Hagi during the pre-match press conference of snubbing the national team - a claim that prompted the midfielder to hit back on Instagram with screenshots of his medical diagnosis and an X-ray of his injured leg.

Ionut Radu also found himself in Hagi's firing line, with the Celta Vigo goalkeeper responding to a similar accusation with a Cristiano Ronaldo-esque 800-word Instagram statement, where he explained that he had been struggling with a shoulder problem for several months.

If the public fallout with his players was not enough, Hagi is also facing accusations of nepotism, with Romanian journalists questioning whether his son, Ianis, has earned his place in the squad on merit.

The 28-year-old has struggled for form at Turkish side Alanyaspor, registering just one assist in 11 appearances this season while spending the entirety of last weekend's game on the substitutes' bench.

With two games remaining, Poland hold a four-point cushion over bottom-placed Romania, meaning a draw on Saturday would be enough to guarantee their League B status.

The Poles will be encouraged by the fact they beat Romania 6-0 during the last international break, although that was just one of two victories Jan Urban's side have recorded in 2026.

Failing to qualify for last summer’s World Cup was a bitter disappointment for the Polish national side, though their subsequent results have left Urban clinging on to his role.

Defeats to Sweden and Bosnia & Herzegovina during the previous international break have ramped up the pressure on the current manager, with the Polish football federation set to make a decision on his future after the next two matches.

Saturday's trip to Bucharest presents a potentially tricky assignment, particularly given that Poland have recorded just two away victories in the last 24 months, both against relatively low-ranked opposition in Malta and Lithuania.

Six defeats in their last nine away matches and just one clean sheet across their previous 10 hardly make for encouraging reading, suggesting Urban's men could have a difficult evening ahead.

As previously mentioned, Romania will be without captain Stanciu and goalkeeper Radu following their injury troubles.

Razvan Marin is also unavailable as the 30-year-old serves his suspension.

In-form Alexandru Cicaldau scored against Bosnia in the previous international break, and the midfielder has since performed well for his club Universitatea Craiova.

Striker Daniel Birligea is expected to lead the attack, having scored two goals in his last three games for Serie A side Frosinone.

Poland are forced to find an alternative option at left back after Przemyslaw Frankowski picked up an injury which is set to rule him out for the entire international break.

Piotr Zielinski and Marcel Regula both missed training after struggling with colds, but both will be a part of the squad in Bucharest.

Robert Lewandowski is expected to lead the attacking efforts, as he looks to add to his impressive tally of eight career goals against Romania - a run which includes successive hat-tricks against the Tricolour.

Hindrich; Bancu, Ilie, Dragusin, Ratiu; Dragomir, Ghita; Coman, Hagi, Man; Birligea

Dragowski; Puchacz, Kiwior, Potulski, Cash; Nowak; Zalewski, Zielinski, Szymanski, Swiderski; Lewandowski

Romania are in the midst of a turbulent time, but Poland’s run of three successive away defeats does not exude much confidence either.

This does not have the makings of a classic under the lights, and our prediction is a 1-1 draw.

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookies' leading candidate to replace under-fire Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach should the latter get sacked.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is expected to get the sack after a poor start

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

However, he has only won three of 15 games in all competitions. Breaking it down even further, the 45-year-old has overseen United's worst top-flight start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 matches.

By Lewis Nolan | 13 Nov 2026 01:32, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 01:32

Liverpool have regularly monitored Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic ahead of the summer transfer window, the latest report has claimed.

The Reds have enjoyed a strong opening to the campaign, with the club fourth in the Premier League, and their only losses in the top flight have come against Arsenal and Manchester City.

Key to the upturn in form has been captain Virgil van Dijk, who has performed well in the heart of defence, helping his side keep four clean sheets.

However, the Dutchman's contract is set to expire at the end of 2026-27, and Andoni Iraola will need a replacement lined up if the 35-year-old leaves.

Journalist Florian Plettenberg has claimed that the Reds are looking closely at Brighton defender Vuskovic, who is valued at €100m (£85m), but the centre-back dreams of joining Real Madrid one day.

Brighton are second in the table with 22 points from a possible 30, and Vuskovic has arguably been the team's best player.

The Croatian is a strong passer, but he most importantly comes out on top in the majority of his individual battles, winning 60% of his duels in the league so far.

Vuskovic is often aggressive with his positioning, and that could make him the perfect partner Jeremy Jacquet, who is more comfortable in a reserved role.

The centre-back is only 19, so he would need time to adapt if he was to sign for the Reds, but he would be an incredible signing.

Van Dijk may still be among the best defenders in the Premier League, but Liverpool cannot continue to rely on the Dutchman forever.

Joe Gomez will likely depart this summer as well, while Ronald Araujo's loan deal from Barcelona may not be made permanent.

That would leave Giovanni Leoni and Jacquet as the only other senior centre-backs at the club, but they will be 20 and 22 respectively by the time next season starts.

While Vuskovic has been exceptional for Brighton, the Reds should consider signing at least two defenders in the summer transfer window in order to address concerns about their depth in defence.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1693. HMRC chase the estate of late ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson for £3.5MILLION in unpaid tax - because he was 'too busy with his ladies to save'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:19 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EST, 10 November 2026

Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) for an outstanding £3.5million in tax owed.

It comes as a result of the estate's inheritance following Eriksson's death in August 2024 due to pancreatic cancer.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last year, the former England manager reportedly had assets worth £4.8m but owed a staggering £7.25m to HMRC alone. He also reportedly had at least £1m outstanding in other debts.

In a bid to help reduce that outstanding debt, his family sold his old mansion called Bjorkefors last year - albeit at a substantial loss.

Eriksson is survived by his son Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39 - from his first marriage to Ann-Christine Pettersson - as well as partner Yaniseth Alcides. During his time as England manager he had a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio.

Speaking to The Sun, Eriksson's lawyer Anders Runebjer has revealed that the estate has no money left to settle the debt - aside from £300,000 in a UK bank and £1m in a Cayman Islands tax haven. He also stated his focus is now to salvage any money for Eriksson's two children after the ex-Three Lions boss had spent his finances around football and women.

Ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased for £3.5million by HMRC

In August 2024, he passed away at the age of 76 following a battle with pancreatic cancer

The Swede is survived by his two children Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39

'Sven earned millions but was always too busy with his football and his ladies to manage money very well,' said Runebjer.

'I told the HMRC I'm not able to get the money in the Cayman Islands or his UK bank and said they're welcome to seize it.

'They replied that they couldn't do that so I told them there was nothing else left - so they won't get paid.

'Sven was regularly sent bills by the British taxman and paid promptly but they changed the rules and now say he still owes £3.5m plus interest after he passed away.

'They're welcome to take whatever they can get but I'm not giving them anything.

'My priority is trying to get whatever money I can that he left for his children - not the British taxman.'

As aforementioned, Eriksson's estate sold his seven-bed house in Torsby, in his native Sweden - located on the banks of Lake Fryken - but at a reduced price.

According to The Sun, the property was on the market for £2m but his family had to lower the price by £400,000 to attract any prospective buyers.

And they went on to add that an anonymous e-commerce businesswoman has now bought it for an undisclosed sum of at least £1.3m - meaning a potential £700,000 loss on market value alone. However, the loss is greater as Eriksson bought the place in 2002 for £4.5m - meaning the true value lost is around £3m.

Last year, Eriksson's former home in Sweden was sold as his family look to reduce debt

Eriksson lived in the property with his partner Yaniseth Alcides until his death

During his time as England boss, he was in a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio

Selling the property was the latest thing Eriksson's family have done in a bid to ease the financial burden they have taken on since his death.

In March 2025, they were forced to auction off his memorabilia - such as a lunch invitation from the late Queen.

Also up for auction was his Armani suit from a 2006 World Cup match with his hand-written team notes still in the pocket.

The 349 items reported to have gone under the hammer for a combined total of £140,000 also include his BBC Coach of the Year trophy in 2001 and a Premier League Manager of the Month award from his time as Manchester City boss.

An Ivory Coast top signed with a special message by former forward Didier Drogba from Eriksson's time as national coach in 2010 was sold as well.

Eriksson was estimated to have received around £7m in pay-offs alone from England, Manchester City and Mexico during his managerial career.

The Swede, who managed England between 2001 and 2006, previously described himself as being 'stupid' with his money.

In one of his last ever interviews, he told The Guardian: 'I was never interested in money - I never took care of it and trusted people to do that for me. I was stupid not to control where the money went. I realised that when I didn't have any more cash!

'I still don't know what I have in the bank.'

#1692. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#1691. Barcelona targeting January move for Tottenham Hotspur defender

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.

The Spanish right-back has attracted attention following his performances for Spain at the World Cup, but Spurs have several reasons to feel confident about keeping hold of the defender.

According to Catalan broadcaster 3Cat, Porro is one of Laporta’s preferred defensive targets as Barcelona consider whether to strengthen their backline in January.

The Catalan club have been dealing with a series of defensive injuries involving Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart. However, Barcelona have not made a final decision on whether to bring in another defender, with the club waiting to assess the injured players’ recoveries.

Laporta’s admiration for Porro reportedly grew during Spain’s World Cup campaign. The Tottenham defender became an important part of the national team, developing a strong understanding with Lamine Yamal on the right flank and scoring twice during the tournament, including in the semi-final against France.

Laporta watched that semi-final in Dallas and was reportedly impressed by Porro’s performance. Barcelona had also gathered information about the defender towards the end of the previous summer transfer window, but their enquiry did not progress into a formal proposal to either the player or Tottenham.

Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a strong negotiating position. The 27-year-old renewed his contract shortly before the World Cup, committing his future to the north London club until 2031.

Reports have also indicated that Tottenham would demand a significant fee to consider allowing the defender to leave. Real Madrid have also been linked with an interest in the Spain international, potentially creating further competition for his signature.

Barcelona’s admiration for Porro is a reminder of the defender’s standing in European football, but there is currently no confirmed bid or formal approach.

Tottenham will be keen to retain a player who remains an important part of their plans. His long-term contract also means the club are under no immediate pressure to negotiate a sale.

The situation could develop if Barcelona decide their defensive injury problems require January reinforcements. For now, however, Spurs remain in a strong position, and any interested club would likely have to make a substantial offer to test their resolve.

#1690. Next Man United manager: Neville urges Pochettino to demand three guarantees before taking the job

By Axel Clody | 13 Nov 2026 07:18

Michael Carrick’s departure from the Manchester United dugout, announced on Thursday morning, has paved the way for the possible arrival of Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford. With the club 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, Manchester United are looking for a change of direction to try to avoid an even more complicated situation this season.

Faced with the possibility of taking over the team, however, the Argentine has received a warning from Gary Neville: do not accept the challenge without concrete guarantees from the board.

The former defender believes Pochettino needs to protect himself before taking the job, particularly given the limitations of the squad and the need for an overhaul. For Neville, INEOS must present a clear commitment to the sporting project, both with regard to immediate signings and planned investment for next season.

Appearing on The Overlap, the Sky Sports pundit pointed to three demands he considers fundamental for the manager: a significant compensation clause in case of dismissal, the signing of two centre-backs in the January window, and a guarantee of a minimum budget to strengthen the squad next summer.

Neville’s first concern relates to the Argentine’s job security.

Pochettino would arrive at Manchester United at a time of deep instability, with the team in a delicate position in the table and under pressure for results. The former player therefore argues that the manager should negotiate significant financial compensation if the club’s executives decide to end his work earlier than planned.

‘If I were Mauricio Pochettino right now, I would be protecting myself with everything I have. He will do that through compensation, so put that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two centre-backs in January.’

The need to reinforce the defensive system, in fact, was one of the points most emphasised by the former Manchester United captain.

Neville believes the area has shortcomings incompatible with the ambitions of a club that wants to return to competing for important positions in the Premier League. In his assessment, Pochettino cannot be held responsible for negative results without being given the conditions to fix the problems found in the squad.

The pundit also highlighted the importance of establishing financial planning in advance for the mid-year transfer window. Signing two defenders in January would therefore not be enough: the Argentine would need to be certain he will receive sufficient resources to continue the overhaul in the following months.

‘So he needs to insist on a minimum budget for next summer’s transfers, so that we can turn this situation around. He needs to insist on receiving a budget that matches his proposal. They have to give him that budget, otherwise he should not accept the job.’

To justify the urgency of changes, Neville pointed to the defensive line-up used by Manchester United in their most recent match: the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. The former player drew attention to the combination of Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven, which finished the match as the team’s back four.

In the pundit’s view, the set-up shows the lack of reliable options and the need for investment in the area. The presence of improvised players or players used out of their usual roles also helps gauge the challenge Pochettino will face if he takes charge of Manchester United.

‘I mean, look at the back four he finished with on Sunday: Dalot at left-back, Mazraoui at right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven. That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League.’

Neville was even more emphatic in showing his disbelief at the state of the squad. For him, it is difficult to find another top-flight team that has finished a match with such a weakened defensive structure.

‘I do not know of any worse back four than that in the Premier League at the moment, if I am watching the games. It is unbelievable that Manchester United finished the game with that back four.’

Ramon has attracted interest after establishing himself at Como. His performances have reportedly caught the attention of several major clubs, with Chelsea among those monitoring his progress.

However, securing his signature may prove complicated because of Real Madrid’s contractual position. The Spanish giants are understood to have retained buy-back and sell-on clauses when Ramon left the club for Como.

Chelsea are also likely to face competition from Arsenal and Manchester United, who have reportedly been linked with the young centre-back.

#1688. Liverpool step up pursuit of 21-year-old Russia international amid interest from Barcelona and PSG

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Liverpool continue to assess potential additions to their attacking options as the club looks towards future transfer windows. One name attracting attention is Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, although the Reds could face serious competition from some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

The 21-year-old has made an impressive start to life in Turkey following his summer move from Lokomotiv Moscow.

His performances have reportedly caught Liverpool’s attention, but Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are also keeping tabs on his situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Liverpool and Arsenal have stepped up their interest in Batrakov after sending scouts to watch him during Galatasaray’s 4-2 Champions League victory over Lille. The Russian midfielder found the net in that match, further strengthening his growing reputation.

Liverpool are not alone in monitoring the youngster. Manchester United, Chelsea and Manchester City have also been credited with interest, while Barcelona and PSG remain potential destinations.

Batrakov joined Galatasaray from Lokomotiv Moscow in August for €25million and has quickly made an impact. The attacking midfielder has reportedly contributed goals in European competition, with his technical quality, creativity and ability to threaten the opposition goal making him an attractive prospect.

One of the most significant details surrounding his future is a reported release clause worth around £50million. The clause is understood to allow him to leave Galatasaray for a club in one of Europe’s top four leagues, potentially giving Liverpool a clear route to pursuing a deal.

However, Galatasaray are reportedly pleased with their summer signing and have little desire to sell him so soon after his arrival.

TEAMtalk also reports that Barcelona have monitored Batrakov for some time, while PSG continue to be viewed as a possible destination. Both clubs could offer strong competition if Liverpool decide to turn their scouting interest into a concrete move.

For Liverpool, Batrakov represents a potential opportunity to secure a highly regarded young attacking midfielder with considerable room for development. His creativity and goal threat could make him an interesting option as the club continues to assess its long-term attacking plans.

The reported £50million release clause provides some clarity over the financial side of a possible transfer. Nevertheless, Liverpool would still need to convince the player that Anfield is the right destination, particularly with Barcelona and PSG reportedly capable of appealing to him.

A January move appears less realistic, with Galatasaray having little interest in losing a player they only signed in the summer. A deal next summer could be a more plausible scenario if Liverpool maintain their interest.

For now, the Reds’ reported scouting activity suggests Batrakov is firmly on their radar, but there is no indication that a formal bid has been submitted. Liverpool will need to continue monitoring his progress before deciding whether to pursue the £50million-rated midfielder.

#1683. Man Utd now facing their own Mo Salah situation as key £55m star 'turns down' latest contract offer

By Lewis Blain | 13 Nov 2026 07:35

Manchester United have suffered another setback in their efforts to secure the long-term future of captain Bruno Fernandes.

The Portugal international has rejected a second contract proposal, with disagreements over salary and the length of an extension preventing an agreement.

The situation presents an early headache for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino, who will be keen to retain one of United's most important players.

According to The Athletic, Fernandes has turned down an improved contract offer from United after rejecting the club's initial proposal in the summer.

Negotiations have been ongoing for several months, but the 32-year-old is yet to receive terms that satisfy him, with both salary and contract length proving key sticking points.

His current agreement expires in June 2027, meaning he could begin discussing a potential free transfer with foreign clubs from January.

United do, however, have the option to extend his deal by a further 12 months, which would protect their position and prevent him from leaving for nothing next summer.

The club remain keen to keep their captain, who was named FWA Footballer of the Year in May and received the PFA Player of the Year award in August after registering a Premier League record of 21 assists last season.

Although his performances have been less consistent this campaign, he remains highly valued at Carrington.

Fernandes is also understood to be considering his future, having previously attracted serious interest from Al-Hilal and Galatasaray. Interestingly, Pochettino wanted to sign the midfielder for Tottenham in 2019, potentially giving the incoming United boss an existing appreciation of his qualities.

The situation has similarities to Liverpool's contract negotiations with Mohamed Salah in early 2025, with a leading player approaching the latter stages of his career and seeking one final major deal.

United are in a delicate position, as they clearly want Fernandes to remain, but must decide whether his requested terms represent sensible business given his age and their efforts to reduce the wage bill.

Equally, the last thing Pochettino needs when arriving at Old Trafford is uncertainty surrounding his captain's commitment and long-term future.

Fernandes has previously indicated that he wants to continue at United, so this is not necessarily a sign that he is pushing for an exit. However, rejecting two proposals suggests the club still have considerable work to do.

United do hold a degree of control through their 12-month extension option, potentially allowing them to protect his transfer value rather than risk losing him for nothing.

Ultimately, finding an agreement should be a priority, but United must avoid allowing the negotiations to become a distraction during another important period of rebuilding.

#1681. Bonera believes Milan Futuro were not ready for first season: “Some thought it was easier”

Daniele Bonera has revisited his time as the head coach of Milan Futuro, revealing his belief that the team wasn’t ready to compete.

The Futuro project was launched ahead of the 2024-25 season to give Milan a ‘second team’ to allow their young talents to develop at a level above that of the Primavera league. They started in Serie C but were relegated in their first season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was taken to sack Bonera as the head coach given the on-field issues, even though they were competing against experienced sides with a very young side. Massimo Oddo followed him, before the club chose to go with Sergio Navarro this summer, who has the Futuro in third.

Bonera was interviewed by Fanpage and he reflected on that period with the B-team and what he learned from it even despite the rough results, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan Futuro was a great opportunity for growth. Perhaps we weren’t clear – and I’m part of this – about the level of Serie C. I had an idea of ​​it, but some thought it was easier,” he said.

“The squad had been built with expectations that were too high compared to what the league is. I don’t think that structure, at that time, was ready to tackle that type of league. On an individual level, however, I felt very comfortable. Starting at home was a positive thing.

“The biggest challenge was understanding which players you actually had available. Some were promoted to the first team, others were dropped, and still others were sent to the Primavera. We had guys who perhaps weren’t playing with us and then came back up.

“From an individual growth perspective, we worked very well in some situations. After a couple of years, we saw the individual value of guys like Camarda, Bartesaghi, Liberali, and Jimenez grow. The value of the players wasn’t in question.

“I think the problem was primarily structural: it’s not always the coach who’s the problem, but the way you do things and the direction you want to take.”
