#1566. Manager of the season is a one-horse race, Man United have taken incompetence to new levels and Newcastle to go down? Our experts' verdict on the Premier League so far

Published: 15:31 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:39 EST, 11 November 2026

With ten games of the Premier League season gone, it's time for another breather as the second international break rolls around. Here's our experts' verdict on the season so far...

Ronald Araujo. The Uruguayan on loan at Liverpool from Barcelona has gone some way to solving a huge problem for Andoni Iraola at right-back. IAN LADYMAN

Pascal Gross – epitome of the Brighton formula. The first signing when they reached the Premier League now back for his second spell. Supreme confidence in the model shines through him. He is understated and over delivering at 35. MATT BARLOW

Martin Odegaard. A sensational footballer. Few players can control those around them in the manner that the Arsenal skipper does, and he is scoring important goals, too. CRAIG HOPE

Brighton's Diego Gomez and Pascal Gross both receive nominations for player of the season so far from Daily Mail Sport's experts

Diego Gomez. You can’t argue with two goal of the season contenders already – one of them from the halfway line. Wonderful midfielder who is integral to how Brighton play. JACK GAUGHAN

Pascal Gross. The Brighton midfielder has covered more ground than any player in the league thus far and is third in the league for goal contributions with eight. A midfield conductor that has hit all the right notes (outside of that one lapse at Anfield with his own goal). NATHAN SALT

Pascal Gross. Three goals, four assists, and such creative and organisational influence from the 35-year-old. He gives Brighton control, finds ways through congested midfields and brings an authority to their pressing game, starting every game and playing more minutes than any team-mate. IAN HERBERT

Declan Rice – Toughie, this. I’ll plump for Rice for his sheer consistency at the heart of an Arsenal side at the top of the table. Mr Reliable. KIERAN GILL

Pascal Gross. Bloke is in his mid-30s, started every Brighton game, has scored four goals, set up another four, meaning only Erling Haaland and Evanilson (an honourable mention for this gong) have combined for more, and has created at least five more chances than any other player in the division. He’s at the heart of everything Brighton do. JAMES SHARPE

Rayan Cherki. Man City’s gifted No10 has been in outstanding form even if his team haven’t. Cherki’s cracking goal in Saturday’s defeat at Nottingham Forest was his seventh of the season on top of three assists. CHRIS WHEELER

Fabian Hurzeler. We are almost a third of the way through the season and Brighton are in second place. The odds are still hugely stacked against them but if they keep up their form, they will be the most unlikely title challengers since Leicester City. OLIVER HOLT

Fabian Hurzeler. We thought Chris Hughton did a good job at Brighton. Ditto Graham Potter and Roberto de Zerbi. But Hurzeler has taken the Seagulls to a different level and all that with the challenge of playing European football thrown in too. Hat tips here also for David Moyes, Keith Andrews, Marco Rose and Sergej Jakirovic. IAN LADYMAN

Fabian Hurzeler – has Brighton in with a genuine chance of a Champions League place as others falter and they continue to build despite selling important players (Baleba & Welbeck) and suffering injuries (Mitoma & Minteh). They play an exciting brand of attractive football, develop young individuals in a team and are handling European football. MATT BARLOW

Fabian Hurzeler. His Brighton team are the best to watch in the division and that is because they are well coached and exact a plan, which opponents are currently unable to combat. Champions League football awaits. CRAIG HOPE

It has to be Fabian Hurzeler. Beaten both Arsenal and Manchester City, hammered Aston Villa and smashed their rivals. Brighton are flying. JACK GAUGHAN

Fabian Hurzeler. Brighton are the Premier League's top scorers, have inflicted Arsenal's only defeat and the Seagulls are flying high as the closest challenger to the Gunners sat in 2nd in the November international break. Marco Rose gets an honourable mention for how well Bournemouth have fared post-Andoni Iraola. NATHAN SALT

Fabian Hurzeler has led Brighton to second place with seven wins from their first ten games

Fabian Hurzeler, Brighton. Yes, he’s working with the players produced by the Tony Bloom data algorithms but he’s adapting those players to games. He didn’t try to outplay Arsenal at their own game, instead making the match chaotic and physically demanding. IAN HERBERT

Fabian Hurzeler – To think a naff Christmas last season prompted claims from your usual In The Knows that Brighton were considering sacking Hurzeler. They stuck with him, and now he has his side sitting second in the Premier League. KIERAN GILL

Fabian Hurzeler. It’s got to be, hasn’t it? He has Brighton second in the Premier League, completely on merit, and fifth in the Conference League. They play beautiful football and are fully in the title race. Some people wanted him sacked last season. JAMES SHARPE

Fabian Hurzeler . Fantastic achievement to guide Brighton to second place in the Premier League a quarter of the way into the season, beating both Arsenal and Manchester City. They are also performing well in the UEFA Conference and won away at Manchester United in the Carabao Cup before going out of the competition to City on penalties. CHRIS WHEELER

Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Brighton. Arsenal are a smooth-running machine. They strengthened well in the summer and are already reaping the rewards. OLIVER HOLT

Arsenal, Man City, Liverpool, Chelsea, Man United. IAN LADYMAN

Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea, Brighton, Spurs. Assuming City are deducted points here I'm backing Liverpool to emerge as closest challengers, Brighton to stay the course and both Spurs and Chelsea to eventually feel the benefit of not being in Europe. MATT BARLOW

Arsenal. Brighton. Manchester City. Liverpool. Chelsea. That is the current order and, Bournemouth apart, I can't see any other team challenging for the top five. Brighton don't have to fall away, as some suggest. They are too well drilled for their position to simply be an upshot of a fast start or momentum. What they have feels more permanent. CRAIG HOPE

Arsenal, Manchester City*, Liverpool, Brighton, Chelsea. City’s second place is pending the fallout of their appeal and any sanctions handed down. Aston Villa and Tottenham will fancy taking a run at the top five but Chelsea and Liverpool should continue improving. Bournemouth are an outside bet too. JACK GAUGHAN

Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Brighton, Chelsea. NATHAN SALT

Arsenal, Liverpool, Brighton, Aston Villa, Chelsea. IAN HERBERT

Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea, Man City, Brighton. Arsenal will win the Premier League, obviously. Manchester City will be distracted by all the chaos. Brighton will sneak a top-five finish with help from their fine start. KIERAN GILL

Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City, Chelsea, Brighton. CHRIS WHEELER

Newcastle United, Coventry City, Ipswich Town. I still think that Newcastle will get sucked into trouble. And I think that the inexperience of their manager will cost them when things get tight. OLIVER HOLT

Man City (deducted points), Crystal Palace, Coventry. Again, a massive guess involved re the City penalty but it's always guesswork even when educated. Isn't it? Fear Coventry will fade and Palace have simply lost too many good players for a managerial change to save them. MATT BARLOW

Hull. Coventry. Crystal Palace. Hull just cannot win enough games and that will catch up with them. Coventry don't have the quality over the course of a season, while Palace look like a side who have lost belief in themselves, their manager and the direction of the club. CRAIG HOPE

Coventry, Ipswich Town, Hull City. While all have enjoyed varying degrees of encouraging starts, the teams around them are either set to change managers or emerging from sluggish form. JACK GAUGHAN

Coventry's defeat at Everton on Friday leaves them one place above the drop zone - and all of our writers are predicting them to go down

Ipswich Town, Coventry City, Crystal Palace. NATHAN SALT

Coventry, Crystal Palace, Sunderland. IAN HERBERT

Crystal Palace, Ipswich, Coventry. Of the three newly-promoted clubs, I’m saying Hull will stay in the Premier League, and Crystal Palace, even with a new manager, will continue to struggle. KIERAN GILL

Coventry, Sunderland, Palace. This is the season Palace go. Only Thomas Frank can save them now. JAMES SHARPE

Daniel Farke. He's been around a long time to be a surprise package but after years of people saying he wasn't good enough to keep a team in the Premier League, his Leeds team is not just surviving but excelling. OLIVER HOLT

I have loved watching Oli McBurnie play for Hull. He leads the line, he sets the tone and he scores the odd goal. A throwback centre-forward. IAN LADYMAN

Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic... given the Tigers a platform they can build on and avoid being drawn into a relegation battle. MATT BARLOW

Bournemouth, their manager Marco Rose and striker Evanilson. I saw them play earlier in the season during a six-match winless league start and, despite that, you knew they would come good. Evanilson (right) has been a revelation for Bournemouth and Marco Rose

Hull City. Widely panned as being the side that would break Derby County's points record en route to an immediate relegation back to the Championship but they've more than held their own so far. Going unbeaten at home to this point is a good sign for survival hopes. NATHAN SALT

Everton. Everton. When their £40million move for Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave them with only one striker, I thought they were done for. Underestimate David Moyes at your peril, I guess, because they’re now sixth in the Premier League. Kudos. KIERAN GILL

Enzo Fernandez. Manchester City fans are starting to realise why some Chelsea supporters were glad to see the back of him, both on the field and off it. OLIVER HOLT

Manchester United. I didn’t expect them to be quite this bad. Michael Carrick and his team have taken incompetence to new levels. IAN LADYMAN

Manchester United. Why complicate it? Even with a change of manager, which is necessary, there is close to no chance they'll recover to qualify again for the Champions League, and for a club of Man United's size there can be no greater underachievement. CRAIG HOPE

Manchester United. They are absolutely shocking from the boardroom to the pitch. Manchester United. Yes, they have been serially failed by owners and have incapable defenders but that league position is beyond all belief. Even this weekend, Bryan Mbeumo and Mason Mount have looked shadows of the players United signed. IAN HERBERT

Bruno Fernandes. Fabulous footballer, obviously, but he has been substandard in what he is providing on the pitch, both as a creator and in his approach to leadership and that is not helping Manchester United right now. KIERAN GILL

Newcastle. Yes, losing Eddie Howe was always going to take some getting used to and, yes, when you look down their team sheet you wonder where all the quality has gone but they shouldn’t be this bad. Opta has them bottom of their expected points table. JAMES SHARPE

Man Utd – from the boardroom to the dressing-room, they are in a mess. Expect United to find some degree of form and move up the table, but this season already feels like a write-off. CHRIS WHEELER

Manchester United. They blew all the momentum Michael Carrick built last season with a desperate summer transfer window. They need to try to remedy that in January. OLIVER HOLT

Tottenham. They need a centre-forward. The rest of the team is starting to look as though it has some balance. IAN LADYMAN

Richarlison's PR team, and Man United still so desperately short of the quality they need in so many key areas. MATT BARLOW

If Brighton qualifying for the Champions League for the first time isn't big enough... maybe Leeds can qualify for Europe. MATT BARLOW

Martin Odegaard is Craig Hope's pick to be named footballer of the year

There could be fewer than five managerial changes through the season – bucking the trend of the last few years. Sage and Michael Carrick both look precarious but others down there seem more settled in their jobs. JACK GAUGHAN

Alexander Isak will dethrone Erling Haaland to win the Golden Boot as Liverpool go closest to Arsenal in the title race. #1565. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1564. Chelsea transfer news: Blues 'boost' in pursuit of Malo Gusto replacement

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 09:39

Chelsea have reportedly received a boost ahead of potentially making an approach for Barcelona defender Jules Kounde.

Xabi Alonso is currently focused on trying to improve the Blues' fifth-placed position in the Premier League table after the November international break.

However, with Malo Gusto said to be open-minded to an exit from Stamford Bridge during the winter transfer window, the Spaniard will assess his options in the market.

When everyone is fit, Chelsea are not short of alternatives at right-back, with Josh Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James all capable of playing in that role.

Nevertheless, as per TEAMtalk, the West Londoners remain attentive to any developments at Camp Nou.

The report suggests that Barcelona will give consideration to ways to generate transfer funds at the turn of the year.

Kounde is allegedly someone who they would think about selling for the right price, while the France international is said to be aware of the situation.

Therefore, Chelsea are seemingly conscious of Kounde - a long-term target for Blues chiefs - becoming available.

He has been restricted to four starts and four substitute outings in all competitions this season, not making an appearance since October 17 due to injury.

Xavi Espart, Joao Cancelo and Brian Farinas are further right-back options for Hansi Flick, highlighting that Barcelona would not necessarily have to spend money to replace Kounde.

While most Chelsea fans would take Kounde as a direct replacement for Gusto, they would not want to add him to the squad if he is going to play ahead of Acheampong.

With the England Under-21 international having emerged as one of Chelsea's best players this season, the Blues fanbase will not want to see his development halted by Kounde.

Therefore, it is questionable whether he should be signed by Alonso, even though he provides cover at centre-back.

All things considered at this point in time, Chelsea should stay out of any race to sign Kounde.

#1562. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision-makers. Unsurprisingly, Matthias Jaissle has named the same starting 11 that beat Tottenham last time out. New signing Matías Fernandez-Pardo is among the substitutes and could make his Premier League debut here.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1561. Real Madrid transfer news: Los Blancos 'set sights' on 18-year-old Brazilian starlet linked to Brighton, Everton

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 10:08

Real Madrid have reportedly identified Atletico Mineiro teenager Vitao as a potential transfer target.

Having reduced the gap to leaders Barcelona in the La Liga table to three points, Jose Mourinho will be content with his start to life back at the Bernabeu.

Furthermore, Los Blancos have improved defensively of late, now having the joint-best such record in Spain's top flight and having conceded three fewer goals than Barcelona.

However, with Antonio Rudiger now 33 years of age and Eder Militao having suffered a number of significant injuries during his career, Real Madrid may soon wish to sign younger alternatives.

According to Sport, club officials have started to assess the development of Brazilian youngster Vitao.

Despite being just 18 years of age, Vitao has already racked up 18 appearances for the Atletico Mineiro first team.

Nine of those outings have come in this season's Brazilian top flight, Vitao most notably scoring in a 3-1 win over Fluminense in September.

At 6ft 4ins and being a three-cap Brazil Under-20 international, the starlet is naturally attracting attention from Europe.

Brighton & Hove Albion are said to be considering whether to make a formal bid for Vitao during the winter transfer window.

Everton are also being linked with a player who allegedly has a €20m (£16.69m) release clause for foreign clubs in his contract.

Although Real Madrid have strength in depth at centre-back, this may be viewed as a tempting market opportunity.

Vitao has just over two years left on his contract and is seemingly destined to make the move to a European club sooner rather than later.

However, he will want to establish a suitable pathway for his development. Signing for Brighton and spending a season on loan in Belgium with Union SG may make more sense than moving to Real Madrid and being used in their Castilla squad.

#1559. IAN HERBERT: Classless Chuckle Brothers Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada are not fit to lace Michael Carrick's boots - they have treated a dignified Man United legend shamefully with this painful charade

Published: 07:34 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:39 EST, 11 November 2026

Both Michael Carrick and the man who has decided to sack him were present on Saturday night at a 40th anniversary dinner for Sir Alex Ferguson, staged in the dining suite where the Old Trafford dressing rooms used to be. It was lost on no one that Carrick, oozing class and humour that evening, spoke far better than Omar Berrada, Manchester United’s chief executive.

There were 100 or so present and Carrick had just been through the wringer of the 3-2 win over Roma but he did not let his predicament obscure the bigger picture. Carrick ‘spoke brilliantly’, actor James Nesbitt, who was also present, related. ‘The Roma result had just happened, but he showed a real gratitude to Sir Alex. He spoke with confidence and humour, but also with a real understanding of the enormity of what he achieved.’

Those who really understand United would not have been surprised. In the days when it was a classy, brilliantly run club, Carrick was the one who, perhaps more than any other senior player, would always look out for the rank-and-file staff – ensuring that the backroom teams were taken out for a drink at the end of the season, and that taxis home were laid on.

It was he who latched on to what was good about the Manchester United ‘family,’ ensuring that everyone from the reception staff to the laundry team were made to feel a part of it. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos have clinically dismantled the old sense of a United ‘community' but Carrick’s return created a gratifying sense around Old Trafford, back in January, that it was perhaps not entirely dead.

All of which contributes to the unalloyed rage that many who love the club will be feeling today about the shameful and classless treatment of Carrick. A man forced through the ritual of driving into the training ground at 7.15am this morning by Berrada and United director of football Jason Wilcox – men not fit to lace his boots – when the whole world knows he is toast.

As Carrick, a professional to his core, went through this painful charade, Berrada and Wilcox – the Statler and Waldorf of the modern Manchester United – had had their secretaries arrange air travel to Monaco today for a meeting with Ratcliffe, which could not be brought forward.

Michael Carrick oozes class and humility but has been dragged through a painful charade by his superiors

Omar Berrada (left) and Jason Wilcox (right) are the the Statler and Waldorf of the modern Manchester United

There have been moments amid the recent tempest which point to United requiring a more commanding manager for the depths that Ratcliffe and his dismal men have reduced the club to. I could see from my vantage point close to the United dugout at their trip to Chelsea, two weeks back, that Carrick simply didn’t have the words to steer the ship away from that afternoon’s disaster.

But in the faces of men like Kobbie Mainoo and, before injury, Marcus Rashford, who have been restored to life and self-belief as United players, we have also witnessed Carrick’s faculty to see and know quality in players and give it full force.

A year ago, we were witnessing Ruben Amorim, the manager hired at vast expense by Ratcliffe’s football geniuses, run down Mainoo’s United career. In the insane mayhem of Sunday afternoon's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, he was the team’s creative anchor.

The people who have actually mattered at United – the fanbase – appreciate the respect Carrick warrants. It’s why the anthem carrying his name was still coming down from the Stretford End and the old North Stand on Sunday.

And so, of course, does Sir Alex, even though you half suspect he wondered all along if Carrick had quite the bite for the toughest job in world football, while hoping against hope he’d thrive.

‘There is a casualness about him that causes people to misunderstand his value and his constitution,’ Ferguson wrote of Carrick in his autobiography. ‘His handicap was, I feel, that he lacked the bravado of Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard. But his character has always been outstanding. He's a football man.’ Sir Alex considered Carrick a better player than both those two.

And now what you suspect will be Carrick’s valedictory days at the club he has served so well are presided over by executives whose own fitness for purpose at Old Trafford was an open question from the start.

Very few people around Manchester City viewed the loss of Berrada, their ‘chief football officer’, as something to be fearful about, when Ratcliffe decided to make him United’s chief executive in 2024. Some former City insiders privately wondered how on earth he’d landed a job of that kind.

‘There is a casualness about him that causes people to misunderstand his value and his constitution,’ Sir Alex Ferguson wrote of Carrick in his autobiography

Sir Alex considered Carrick a better player than both Frank Lampard and Steven Gerrard

United want to tell Carrick ‘face to face’ what the whole world knows. These people won’t even discern what gross disrespect they are affording a man who deserves far better

And if Ratcliffe thought he was accessing City’s intellectual property when recruiting Jason Wilcox as technical director, then that was dodgy logic, too. Wilcox had only run City’s academy – a grossly incomparable challenge. His comparable experience to the United role was a mere 15 months as Southampton’s director of football. They were in the Championship for some of that time.

These were the men jetting out to Ratcliffe’s tax haven to tell him who should and should not manage United. Thus subjecting Carrick to another phantom training session at the Carrington – two weeks after watching the Under 21s play there while those Chuckle Brothers put their heads together about sacking him, across the complex.

United are putting it around, would you believe, that they want to be seen to be ‘doing the right thing’ and ‘observing the right process’. Well frankly, many inside football view this leadership group’s decision making as an embarrassment.

Nesbitt expressed sympathy for Carrick. ‘I feel for him,’ he said. ‘I'm no pundit but I am a fan. Clearly there's dissatisfaction with the fans about what we perceive is going on, but I think he's trying his best.’

United want to tell Carrick ‘face to face’ what the whole world knows. These people won’t even discern what gross disrespect they are affording a man who deserves far better.

#1558. Arsenal's Jurrien Timber lauded by Dutch media for attacking "masterclass" in Netherlands 7-0 Greece

By Ben Knapton | 14 Nov 2026 10:22

Arsenal's Jurrien Timber was the star of the show as the Netherlands demolished Greece 7-0 in Friday's UEFA Nations League affair, and the Dutch media did not hold back in their praise of the defender.

The 25-year-old has experienced a mildly frustrating start to the 2026-27 season overall, starting just three Premier League games due to his long-term groin injury and the strong form of Ben White.

Timber played the full 90 in both of Arsenal's last two top-flight wins against Liverpool and Hull City before the international break, though, and he started at left-back when the Netherlands hosted Greece, with Denzel Dumfries operating on the right.

Timber earned his shot thanks to Virgil van Dijk's withdrawal, which saw Micky van de Ven shifted into a central role, but the former Ajax man repaid Xavi's faith in him with his first two goals for his country.

Timber had failed to score in any of his first 25 Netherlands appearances, but the defender tapped home his maiden senior international goal in the 40th minute from close range, before netting his second and his country's sixth at the far stick from Dumfries's ball across.

The Arsenal man put in a "flawless" display, according to Soccernews, who awarded him a perfect 10/10 rating and also praised his two pre-assists and the "ability to play anywhere".

Mee met Oranje held off on giving Timber full marks, but the 25-year-old was nevertheless handed a 9/10 as the "most striking" player on the field, delivering an "exceptional" performance that left Greece unable to get a hold on him.

Voetbal Primeur highlighted Xavi calling Timber the "perfect joker" in the lead-up to the game and claimed that the defender fulfilled that role to perfection, while operating more like a "half number 10" when attacking.

The same outlet also handed Timber a nine out of 10 for a Nations League "masterclass", as the Netherlands moved three points clear at the top of the League A Group 2 standings.

Timber is no stranger to playing as a left-back for Arsenal, featuring there 14 times in his Gunners career, but Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie are currently battling for minutes on that side.

Calafiori in particular has embraced a free bird role at left-back, often popping up in central attacking areas, while Timber has been more widely lauded for his 1v1 defensive prowess.

However, the Dutchman has now demonstrated a Calafiori-esque strength to his play, offering Arteta an intriguing and highly useful alternative from a tactical and fitness sense.

Timber at left-back allows the Arsenal boss to rotate Gabriel Magalhaes with Calafiori and/or Hincapie, so long as White also steers clear of injury and maintains his standout form.

Timber and the Netherlands' next assignment comes away to Germany on Monday, and Xavi's side need just a point to be sure of a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

#1557. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1556. GdS: January arrivals and a return to the top – Cardinale’s strategy to land van Dijk

Gerry Cardinale wants to return AC Milan to the top and he hopes that adding another elite player next summer will help to achieve that goal.

With the signing of Luka Modric, and the subsequent quality that he’s shown since, Milan may tap into the experienced free agent market more. Of course, opportunities have to be right, but Cardinale is becoming more in favour of signing these types of players.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, in the summer, they may look to Anfield instead of the Bernabeu, where Virgil van Dijk could become the new Luka Modric.

Calciomercato.com relays words from Gazzetta dello Sport, building on their report this morning of the interest in van Dijk. The move, it seems, would be pushed for by Cardinale and the American is already working up a plan.

In January, the Rossoneri will strengthen the defence, with Goncalo Inacio and Massire Sylla the favoured names currently. With these additions, the American would hope for a return to the Champions League, which would be essential to signing van Dijk.

So, with the mix of promising youth recruited in January, they would hope to finalise the defensive transformation with a world-class player next season. Cardinale remains convinced of van Dijk’s quality, and he can discuss a move as early as February 1.

With no sign of the stalemate at Anfield ending, the American – who holds a stake in Liverpool’s ownership – remains hopeful.

#1555. Kazakhstan vs Slovakia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 11:32

Slovakia square off against Kazakhstan on Monday having already secured top spot in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

In sharp contrast to the visitors earning promotion with a game to spare, Kazakhstan must win this fixture to have any chance of avoiding finishing bottom of the group.

Ranked highest in the FIFA World Rankings, Slovakia were the clear favourites to win this group, and Vladimir Weiss's side have delivered.

Despite failing to win either match against Faroe Islands, scoring eight goals across victories in the other games has given them a four-point lead with one fixture left.

On a negative note, Slovakia have only kept clean sheets versus Moldova, something which will serve as added motivation for his contest.

Although they came from behind to earn a 2-2 draw at home to Faroe Islands on Friday, Slovakia extended their unbeaten record in all competitions to eight games.

Meanwhile, Slovakia have scored at least two goals in all but one of those encounters.

As for Kazakhstan, they have now gone seven matches without recording a win, their last success coming against Comoros on March 31.

Like their next opponents, failing to emerge victorious from either fixture versus Faroe Islands was a major disappointment, but they have not helped themselves with red cards in the last two games.

John van 't Schip's team went down 2-1 in Moldova on Friday, ending their hopes of finishing in the top two.

However, victory on Monday would keep them in the hunt of finishing third, with Faroe Islands also needing to lose to Moldova to keep their chances alive.

Kazakhstan have scored and conceded in each of their last seven games.

Having lost out to a 77th-minute goal on Friday, Van 't Schip may be against making many changes to his Kazakhstan XI.

However, Sergey Maliy has served a one-match ban and could replace Temirlan Erlanov in the middle of the back three.

Yan Vorogovskiy may get the nod over Nauryzbek Zhagorov at left wing-back, a result of replacing him at half time versus Moldova.

Slovakia will make a change at right-back with Martin Valjent serving a one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

Tobias Paliscak is in line to come into the team, while Weiss will consider making further alterations with top spot secured.

Centre-back Ivan Mesik, centre-midfielder Matus Bero and forward Robert Bosenik could all b handed opportunities.

#1554. Police 'are trawling through dodgy Fire Stick sellers' bank accounts to contact illegal viewers' of Premier League football and films

Published: 11:08 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:40 EST, 11 November 2026

A former detective has revealed the lengths authorities are going to in order to crack down on the use and sale of 'dodgy Fire Sticks'.

Law enforcement organisations across the UK are taking a tougher stance on these devices – and how they are used and distributed – with multiple people having been convicted and jailed in recent years for selling and supplying them.

The devices, which often cost anywhere between £30 and £100 – in comparison with around £30 a month for a Sky Sports subscription – give customers access to a range of premium TV services without paying, most notably in a football sense with access to live matches.

But Rav Wilding, a former detective who recently appeared on the BBC Morning Live show, has sent a fresh warning to individuals that use them.

Wilding said: 'People are buying them online usually on the black market and then they're getting all these services for free essentially.

'But it's a crime. It's not allowed. Owning the stick itself is not a crime, but using it for this purpose is.'

A former detective has revealed the lengths authorities are going to in order to crack down on the use and sale of 'dodgy Fire Sticks'

Wilding went on to say that along with a crackdown on sellers through house raids, authorities are now looking through their accounts to find out in further detail who is using the devices.

They then often contact those users in a new step, with it estimated that around four million people or households have got these Fire Sticks at the moment.

Wilding added: 'All of them are using them illegally. They're going for the distributors. They're going for the sellers. They are having a lot of success. But actually, once they've got the seller, they're going through their accounts.

'They're seeing who has been paying the money for these illegal things, and if they've been paying them for these sticks then people should possibly expect a conversation or two if the police want to know why they've been paying them money for this.'

Wilding revealed that this included checking bank statements to find out the information of individuals who have been paying for such a service, and authorities have been joined by subscription service providers in their clampdown attempts too.

'They (subscription service providers) are losing money to this, so they have been reaching out and are taking action against those people using them illegally as well,' he explained.

'So I wouldn't say it's something you should do. It is actually a crime and it can have a nasty fine, a huge fine and also a custodial sentence for users and sellers of these things.'

Rav Wilding appeared on BBC Morning Live and sent a fresh warning to users of the devices

Daily Mail Sport has previously reported FACT is playing a leading role in the crackdown on the devices, with the anti-piracy organisation liaising with police forces across the country.

And Kieron Sharp, chairman of FACT, added: 'We have a wide range of enforcement options - from issuing cease and desist notices to "knock and talk" visits - through to full criminal prosecutions where appropriate.

'We will take robust action against those involved - not only targeting sellers and distributors, but also those facilitating and profiting from the illegal activity.'

#1553. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”
